accident_page.title: Road Traffic Accident
accident_page.warning: ⚠️ Road traffic accident: react quickly and methodically.

protect.title: 1. Protect
protect.step1: Secure the area with warning triangles, hazard lights, etc.
protect.step2: Assess dangers such as moving vehicles, fire, etc.

alert.title: 2. Alert
alert.step1: Call emergency services (118 for Fire Department, 101 for Emergency Medical Services).
alert.step2: Provide precise information: Exact location, number of victims, type of injuries, potential dangers.

rescue.title: 3. Rescue
rescue.step1: Unconscious victim who is breathing: Place in recovery position (PLS).
rescue.step2: Victim who is not breathing: Start CPR and use a defibrillator if available.
rescue.step3: Victim with severe bleeding: Compress the wound and apply a tourniquet if necessary.
rescue.step4: Victim with trauma: Maintain head-neck-trunk alignment.

reassure.title: 4. Reassure
reassure.step1: Speak calmly to victims to reassure them and explain what you are doing while waiting for emergency services.

cpr.title: Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation
cpr.step1:
Chest compressions:
- Place hands in the center of the chest.
- Arms straight, press hard (5 cm) and fast (100 to 120/min).
- Release after each compression.
cpr.step2:
Mouth-to-mouth:
- Tilt the head, pinch the nose.
- Give 2 breaths (the chest should rise).

pls.title: Recovery Position
pls.step1: Kneel beside the victim lying on their back.
pls.step2: Place the nearest arm at a right angle, palm facing up.
pls.step3: Bring the other arm and place the back of the hand against their cheek, on the rescuer's side.
pls.step4: Grab the opposite leg behind the knee and bend it.
pls.step5: Gently pull on the bent leg to roll the victim towards you.
pls.step6: Adjust so that the leg is at a right angle and the head is **stable** tilted back.
pls.step7: Mouth turned towards the ground to prevent choking.
pls.step9: If possible, position the victim on their left side.

additional_info.title: Additional Information
additional_info.step1: Prevention: Follow traffic rules, stay alert and avoid unnecessary risks.
additional_info.step2: Psychological aspects: Be attentive to the emotional state of victims and witnesses, the accident can be traumatic.

cardiac_arrest.title: Cardiac Arrest
cardiac_arrest.alert_banner: Alert: Acting quickly is essential in case of cardiac arrest. Call 101 (Emergency Medical Services) immediately and follow instructions.
cardiac_arrest.protection_banner: Protection: Ensure your safety and that of the victim before intervening. Avoid any potential danger.

adult.title: 🧍 Adult Case
adult.step2: Check consciousness: speak to the victim, tap shoulders.
adult.step3: Check breathing: tilt head back + lift chin. Observe for 10 seconds.
adult.step6: Rescue breaths: 2 rescue breaths if trained.

infant.title: 👶 Infant Case (< 1 year)
infant.step2: Stimulate gently: tap the soles of feet.
infant.step3: Check breathing: gentle head tilt, observe.
infant.step6: 30 compressions with 2 fingers at center of chest.

aed.title: ⚡ AED Usage
aed.step1: Turn on the AED and follow voice instructions.
aed.step2: Attach electrodes to the victim's bare chest.
aed.step3: Ensure no one touches the victim during analysis and shock.
aed.step4: Deliver shock if AED recommends it.

burns.definition_text: A burn corresponds to partial or total destruction of the skin. It is considered serious when its surface exceeds half the palm of the victim's hand
burns.before_acting_step1: Contact emergency services immediately at 101 (SAMU) and follow the instructions.
burns.before_acting_step2: Ensure your safety and that of the victim before intervening. Avoid any potential danger
burns.simple_burns_step1: Redness or small blister (less than half the palm).
burns.simple_burns_step2: Rinse abundantly with cold water (Apply the rule of 15, see rule above)
burns.simple_burns_step5: Consult a doctor for a child or infant.
burns.serious_burns_step1: Surface > half the palm, sensitive areas (face, hands, joints), or blackish appearance.
burns.serious_burns_step3: Cool with cold water without pressure (Apply the rule of 15, see rule above)
burns.serious_burns_step4: Lay the victim on a clean sheet.
burns.serious_burns_step5: Do not tear off clothes stuck to the skin.
burns.rule_15_text: 15 minutes under a water jet, at 15°C (cold tap water), at 15 cm distance.
burns.warning_message: ⚠️ Never apply fatty substances, ointments or other products to a burn without medical advice.

electrocution.emergency_warning: ⚠️ VITAL EMERGENCY – Never intervene without securing the area!
electrocution.secure_zone_step1: Do not touch the victim if they are still in contact with electricity.
electrocution.secure_zone_step2: Immediately cut off the power (circuit breaker, fuse or socket).
electrocution.secure_zone_step3: Use a non-conductive object to push away the source (wood, dry cloth, plastic).
electrocution.secure_zone_step4: Make sure the area is safe before acting.
electrocution.alert_emergency_step2: Give details about the incident and the victim's condition.
electrocution.first_aid_step1: If the victim is not breathing: start CPR (30 compressions + 2 breaths if trained).
electrocution.first_aid_step2: Cool burns with cold water for 10 minutes.
electrocution.first_aid_step3: Remove clothing not stuck to the burn.
electrocution.first_aid_step4: Protect the burn with a clean cloth or sterile bandage.

alert_message: Alert: Act quickly in case of choking. Call emergency services (101 SAMU).
protection_message: Protection: Priority to your safety for effective help.
general_info_step_1: Choking is an obstruction of the airways often caused by food or an object.
general_info_step_2: It can be partial (the person coughs) or total (they can no longer breathe, speak or cough).
partial_obstruction_step_1: Leave the person in the position where they feel most comfortable.
partial_obstruction_step_3: Do not intervene with back blows or compressions.
partial_obstruction_step_4: Monitor breathing and call a doctor if necessary.
total_obstruction_step_1: Give 5 back blows between the shoulder blades.
total_obstruction_step_2: If the object doesn't come out, perform 5 abdominal compressions (Heimlich maneuver).
total_obstruction_step_3: Alternate back blows and compressions until clearance or loss of consciousness.
total_obstruction_step_4: If the person loses consciousness, alert emergency services and begin cardiopulmonary resuscitation.
infant_step_1: Place the infant face down on your forearm, head lower than the body.
infant_step_3: Turn the infant over and perform 5 chest compressions.
infant_step_5: Never perform the Heimlich maneuver on an infant.
technique_step_1:
➡️ Clearance by back blows:
- Give 5 blows between the shoulder blades with the flat of an open hand.
- In children, tilt the head lower than the body (for example, over a knee).
- In infants, place them face down on the forearm, head low, and support the head without pressing on the throat.
technique_step_2:
➡️ Clearance by abdominal compressions:
- Stand behind the victim.
- Pass your arms under theirs, place a fist just above the navel.
- Grasp the fist with the other hand.
- Pull sharply towards yourself and upward.
- Same for adults and children, never for infants.
technique_step_3:
➡️ Clearance by chest compressions:
- To be performed on infants or if abdominal compressions are impossible.
- Place the victim on their back on a hard surface.
- Kneel down and perform 5 chest compressions.
- If unconscious: begin CPR with 30 compressions at 100–120/min.
final_warning: ⚠️ If the obstruction persists or if the victim loses consciousness, call emergency services immediately (101 SAMU)!

stay_calm.title: Stay calm and assess the situation
stay_calm.text: Keep your calm. Check if the victim is conscious and avoid moving the injured limb.

alert_protection.title: Alert and Protection
alert_protection.text: Protect yourself, secure the area if necessary, then immediately contact emergency services (Emergency: 911).

stabilize_head.title: Stabilize the head if cervical trauma
stabilize_head.text: Stabilize the victim's head in case of cervical trauma (See: Head Immobilization).

immobilize_area.title: Immobilize the affected area
immobilize_area.text: Use a board, magazine, or any other rigid object to stabilize the limb. Do not attempt to reset the bone.

apply_cold.title: Apply cold
apply_cold.text: Apply ice or a cold cloth for 20 minutes to limit swelling. Take a break before repeating.

no_massage.title: Do not massage or heat
no_massage.text: Do not apply massage or heat for the first 48 hours, as this could worsen the injury.

consult_professional.title: Consult a healthcare professional
consult_professional.text: Even if the pain seems mild, a medical evaluation is essential for appropriate treatment.

nutrition_care.title: Take care of nutrition
nutrition_care.text: Consume foods rich in protein, vitamin D and C to promote bone healing.

prepare_rehabilitation.title: Prepare for rehabilitation
prepare_rehabilitation.text: Physiotherapy is often necessary. Follow medical advice carefully to regain your mobility.

final_message: 📝 Good reflexes and quick reaction can make all the difference in case of fracture!

main_title: Actions to take in case of drowning
steps_0: Remove the victim from the water if possible, without endangering yourself.
steps_2: Check if the victim is breathing by clearing the airway.
steps_3: If the victim is not breathing, start cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR).
steps_4: Continue CPR until emergency services arrive or breathing resumes.
steps_5: If available, cover the victim with an emergency blanket.
steps_6: Note the exact time when the victim was removed from the water.
airway_content:
Place one hand on the victim’s forehead.
• With the other hand, place your fingertips under the tip of the chin.
• Gently tilt the head back while lifting the chin.
cpr_content:
Chest compressions:
- Place your hands in the center of the chest.
- Keep arms straight, press hard (5 cm) and fast (100 to 120/min).
- Release after each compression.
Mouth-to-mouth:
- Tilt the head back, pinch the nose.
- Give 2 breaths (the chest should rise).
Alternate 30 compressions / 2 breaths.
main_description: 🧠 React quickly to loss of consciousness.
definition_content: A person is considered to have lost consciousness when they do not respond or react to any stimulus, but they are still breathing.
immediate_action_2: If alone, start CPR before calling.
immediate_action_3: Lay the victim on their back on a hard surface.
immediate_action_4: Clear the airway: tilt the head back and lift the chin.
immediate_action_5: Ensure your safety: never intervene by putting yourself in danger.
conduct_1: Check for unresponsiveness: ask a simple question, gently shake the shoulders.
conduct_2: Lay the victim on their back if they don't respond.
conduct_5: Check breathing for a maximum of 10 seconds by leaning over the victim, with the rescuer's ear and cheek above the victim's mouth and nose to observe if the belly and chest rise, listen for any sounds caused by breathing, and feel any airflow during expiration
conduct_6: - If breathing: place in recovery position (see section below).
conduct_7: - If not breathing: doesn't speak and doesn't react (no chest or belly movement, no breath felt at nose or mouth), start CPR.
conduct_8: Monitor breathing until emergency services arrive.

definition_1: A wound is an opening in the skin.
definition_2: It can be simple, deep, dirty, or contain a foreign object.
definition_3: Some wounds can cause significant bleeding.
actions_1: Wear gloves or protect yourself with a plastic bag.
actions_2: Observe the wound without touching it directly.
actions_3: Do not remove a foreign object stuck in the wound.
actions_4: Compress with a clean cloth if it bleeds.
actions_5: Lay the victim down if they feel unwell.
actions_6: Alert emergency services if the wound is serious.
actions_7: Monitor the victim until help arrives.
dont_do_1: Do not apply any product on the wound.
dont_do_2: Do not try to clean a deep wound on site.
dont_do_3: Do not directly compress a wound with an embedded object.
bleeding_subtitle: 🩸 React effectively to a bleeding situation.
definition_contentt: Bleeding is the flow of blood out of the blood vessels. It can be external (visible) or internal (not visible).
alert_protection_points: Immediately alert emergency services: SAMU (101), Firefighters (118).
If you are alone and must call for help, quickly apply a temporary dressing if possible to free your hands.
If available, put on protective gloves.
Wash your hands thoroughly after the intervention.
direct_compression_points: Apply direct pressure to the wound using a compress or clean cloth.
The cloth should completely cover the wound.
Replace your hand with a temporary dressing if necessary.
Use a wide band, long enough to wrap several times, and tight enough to maintain pressure.
tourniquet_points: Use if direct compression is ineffective and the bleeding is very heavy.
Place the tourniquet between the wound and the heart.
Tighten until the bleeding stops completely.
Use an industrial tourniquet if available, following the manufacturer's instructions.
warning_text: ⚠️ These actions are first aid measures and do not replace certified training. Always call emergency services in serious situations.
